claim: Rosiglitazone increases the risk of myocardial infarction
gold_rationale: This is the archetypal contested drug-safety signal. The 2007 Nissen-Wolski meta-analysis (NEJM, 42 trials) reported a statistically significant increase in MI (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.03-1.98, P=0.03) and drove FDA action (2007 boxed warning; 2010 REMS restrictions). The 2010 updated meta-analysis (56 trials, Arch Intern Med) reproduced a significant MI signal (OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.02-1.63) though cardiovascular mortality was never significant (OR 1.03). However, the only large dedicated cardiovascular-outcomes RCT, RECORD (Lancet 2009), found MI HR 1.14 (95% CI 0.80-1.63) — NOT statistically significant — and no increase in overall CV morbidity/mortality (though it confirmed a real heart-failure signal). The FDA then mandated an independent Duke/DCRI readjudication of RECORD (results published Am Heart J 2013, PMID:23895806), which reproduced the original RECORD findings (MI HR 1.13, 95% CI 0.80-1.59; composite HR 0.95) and did not confirm an elevated ischemic risk, leading the FDA in November 2013 to remove the REMS/prescribing restrictions and an FDA advisory committee to reassess the signal. The meta-analyses (dominated by short trials, sparse events, and susceptible to how zero-event trials are handled) point one way; the dedicated long-term RCT and its independent readjudication point the other. Consensus therefore is genuinely CONTESTED: a real, influential, but non-robust MI signal that a dedicated trial and regulatory readjudication substantially walked back — while heart failure (a different outcome) is the one confirmed cardiovascular harm.
provenance: Adversarially re-verified 2026-07-08: five PMIDs confirmed via PubMed get_article_metadata (titles/design/N/effect estimates verbatim); FDA 2013 REMS removal confirmed via FDA drug safety communication + contemporaneous reporting. Row 5 source_id corrected from methodology paper (23895802) to results paper (23895806).
notes: No retractions on any cited PMID (all normal article types). RECORD (19501900) correctly marked population_match=true despite contradicting the claim — conflicting trial not suppressed. dramatic_effect=false throughout is correct (ordinary effect sizes; a randomized trial contradicts the signal).

baseline.text: Yes. Rosiglitazone has been associated with an increased risk of myocardial infarction in patients with type 2 diabetes. The landmark 2007 Nissen and Wolski meta-analysis in NEJM pooled 42 trials and found a significant ~43% relative increase in MI (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.03-1.98), which prompted an FDA boxed warning and prescribing restrictions. A 2010 updated meta-analysis reproduced the MI signal. However, the finding is contested: the dedicated RECORD cardiovascular-outcomes trial did not find a statistically significant increase in MI, and a later FDA-mandated readjudication led the FDA to lift the restrictions in 2013. The most consistently confirmed cardiovascular harm is heart failure, not MI.

rows.citation: Nissen SE, Wolski K. Effect of rosiglitazone on the risk of myocardial infarction and death from cardiovascular causes. N Engl J Med. 2007;356(24):2457-71. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa072761
rows.integrity_note: Landmark signal-generating meta-analysis; limitation acknowledged by authors (no patient-level source data, fixed-effects, sparse events, exclusion of zero-event trials).
rows.finding: 42 trials; MI OR 1.43 (95% CI 1.03-1.98, P=0.03) and CV death OR 1.64 (95% CI 0.98-2.74, P=0.06). SUPPORTS claim on the exact claimed outcome (MI). Verbatim-verified against PubMed abstract.

rows.citation: Nissen SE, Wolski K. Rosiglitazone revisited: an updated meta-analysis of risk for myocardial infarction and cardiovascular mortality. Arch Intern Med. 2010;170(14):1191-1201. DOI:10.1001/archinternmed.2010.207
rows.integrity_note: Updated 56-trial pooled analysis; MI signal persists but CV mortality not significant, tempering the harm narrative.
rows.finding: 56 trials, 35,531 patients (19,509 rosiglitazone); MI OR 1.28 (95% CI 1.02-1.63, P=0.04) — SUPPORTS. CV mortality OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.78-1.36, P=0.86) — NOT elevated. Verbatim-verified against PubMed abstract.

rows.citation: Home PD, Pocock SJ, Beck-Nielsen H, et al. Rosiglitazone evaluated for cardiovascular outcomes in oral agent combination therapy for type 2 diabetes (RECORD): a multicentre, randomised, open-label trial. Lancet. 2009;373(9681):2125-35. DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(09)60953-3
rows.integrity_note: Only large dedicated CV-outcomes RCT; open-label design and lower-than-expected event rate limit power, but it directly tests the MI outcome and did NOT confirm the signal. Confirmed a real heart-failure harm (distinct outcome). Correctly marked population_match=true despite contradicting the claim.
rows.finding: 4447 patients (2220 rosiglitazone), mean 5.5y follow-up; MI HR 1.14 (95% CI 0.80-1.63) — NOT significant. No increase in overall CV morbidity/mortality. CONTRADICTS the significant-MI claim; heart failure HR 2.10 (95% CI 1.35-3.27, confirmed). Verbatim-verified against PubMed abstract.

rows.citation: Home PD, Pocock SJ, Beck-Nielsen H, et al. Rosiglitazone evaluated for cardiovascular outcomes — an interim analysis. N Engl J Med. 2007;357(1):28-38. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa073394
rows.integrity_note: Unplanned interim analysis of RECORD published to address the 2007 controversy; explicitly underpowered for MI.
rows.finding: Interim RECORD: data insufficient to determine MI effect; no significant difference in MI or CV/all-cause death; heart-failure risk increased (HR 2.15, 95% CI 1.30-3.57). NULL/inconclusive on the claimed MI outcome. Verbatim-verified against PubMed abstract.

rows.citation: Mahaffey KW, Hafley G, Dickerson S, et al. (Home PD, Lopes RD). Results of a reevaluation of cardiovascular outcomes in the RECORD trial. Am Heart J. 2013;166(2):240-249.e1. DOI:10.1016/j.ahj.2013.05.004
rows.integrity_note: FDA-requested independent Duke/DCRI blinded re-adjudication of RECORD CV endpoints; the reanalysis reproduced the original RECORD findings and did not confirm elevated ischemic risk, underpinning the FDA's Nov-2013 removal of rosiglitazone REMS/prescribing restrictions. source_id corrected from the companion methodology paper (PMID:23895802) to this results paper, which carries the actual readjudicated effect estimates.
rows.finding: Independent FDA-mandated re-ascertainment/readjudication of RECORD endpoints (25,833 person-years, +328 added): MI HR 1.13 (95% CI 0.80-1.59) and composite CV-death/MI/stroke HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.78-1.17), consistent with original RECORD (no confirmed excess ischemic risk), leading FDA to lift restrictions. CONTRADICTS a robust MI-harm conclusion. Verbatim-verified against PubMed abstract.
